## #3 Glamorise MagicLift Natural Shape Support Bra (Style 1010): Best wireless bra for teardrop shape in extended sizing


The Style 1010 earns its place on a teardrop-specific list through one construction detail: a diagonal seam across the cup. Most wireless bras use horizontal or vertical seam placement.


A horizontal seam divides the cup at the fullest point of the breast rather than following the contour. A diagonal seam runs in a direction that mirrors the natural curve of a bottom-full, projected breast, accommodating forward projection more naturally without a wire.


This is also the list's extended-sizing pick. Bands run from 36 to 50, and cups from B through I. That range covers women who are underserved by most bra lines. At $59, the construction is wireless with full-cup coverage.


Reviewers consistently praise the natural shape the bra creates, especially women with bottom-heavy breast shapes who found that molded cups distort their silhouette rather than follow it. Comfort and all-day wearability come up frequently.


The honest tradeoff: negative reviews cluster at the larger end of the size range, specifically at 42G and above. Multiple reviewers report rolling at the band and loss of cup support over extended wear. Readers at 42G and above should expect a shorter wear lifespan and may find the structure insufficient for high-projection shapes at that volume.


Best for:


Women with teardrop breast shape in extended sizes who want a wireless option with seam construction built for bottom fullness and projection, at a lower price point.


## #4 Leonisa Convertible Balconette Lace Push-Up Bra: Best balconette-style pick for teardrop shape with defined lift


A balconette cup is cut horizontally across the top, creating a low, wide cup opening. For a bottom-full, projected breast, that geometry distributes the cup's volume toward the lower portion, which can follow the actual shape of the breast more naturally than a full-coverage cup that tries to contain tissue evenly in all directions. That is the structural argument for this style.


The tension: a balconette on a highly projected shape can gap at the outer edge or fail to contain the breast at the sides. This Leonisa style partially addresses that with a convertible strap system. Crossing the straps changes the angle at which the cup is pulled upward and inward, which can improve how a balconette tracks against a projected breast.


Priced at $60, the size range is limited to 34-36B. The balconette cut pairs with a lace overlay and a push-up effect. Straps convert between straight and crossed configurations.


Reviewers praise the design, quality, and comfort. Customers describe "great support and style" and "perfect lift."


Sizing is inconsistent, though. Some found it runs small while others felt it was too large. Several shoppers noted discomfort from seams and stitching on the back, and the multiple-hook closure was difficult to fasten alone.


The primary caveat for teardrop wearers: the push-up element. Women with significant forward projection may find that additional push-up padding amplifies projection to an uncomfortable degree or creates fit pressure at the cup's outer edge. If forward projection is already your dominant fit variable, adding more of it with padding may not be the answer.


Best for:


Teardrop-shaped wearers in smaller cup sizes who want a balconette silhouette with defined lift, tolerate or want some push-up effect, and are comfortable verifying sizing against a non-standard fit chart.

## **Do you have a teardrop breast shape?**


Still having trouble figuring out your breast shape? Here’s a quick and easy checklist to find out if you are the owner of teardrop shaped breasts.


1. Your breasts are fuller at the bottom of the cup.


2. Your nipples face upward when standing straight.


3. The majority of your breast tissue sits below the nipple.


4. Your breasts resemble the shape of a teardrop.


One additional way you can test to see if you have teardrop breasts is to bend over in front of a mirror at a 90 degree angle without a bra. If your nipple sits on the upper part of the breast, this is an indication of teardrop breasts.


## **The difference between teardrop and bell shape**


Teardrop breasts are often confused with[bell shaped](https://www.honeylove.com/blogs/bra-talk/the-best-bras-for-bell-shaped-breasts-a-comprehensive-guide) breasts, which can be similar in appearance but have some distinct differences. While both shapes are known for bottom fullness, a teardrop breast will typically have the majority of the breast tissue sitting below the nipple. A bell shape, by contrast, will typically have a more slender build at the top of the breast, and the nipple may sit fairly low.


## **Fit issues for teardrop breasts**


Because of the distribution of tissue on a teardrop breast, this shape can create gapping around the top cup of the bra, particularly around the strap platform. The biggest[fit issue](https://www.honeylove.com/blogs/bra-talk/the-ultimate-bra-sizing-guide) is finding a bra style that fits both the top and bottom of the breast. If you’re experiencing these problems when it comes to fit, that is also a clue that you may have teardrop breasts.


## **Recommended bra styles for teardrop breasts**


The best bra for people with teardrop breast shapes are bras that have flexible construction and can conform to the natural shape of the breast.


### Balconette bra


[Balconette bras](https://www.honeylove.com/blogs/bra-talk/what-is-a-balconette-bra) have a lower cut and a horizontal neckline, providing lift and shaping, which can complement the teardrop shape.


### Push-up bra


[Push-up bras](https://www.honeylove.com/blogs/bra-talk/push-up-bras-vs-padded-bras-whats-the-difference) with padding at the bottom can enhance cleavage and provide lift, creating a more rounded appearance at the top of the breasts.


### Plunge bra


Plunge bras with a lower center gore are suitable for lower-cut tops and can enhance the natural teardrop shape.


###
Demi bra


Demi bras have a lower cut and less coverage, allowing the top of the breasts to be more visible while still providing support.


## Bras for teardrop breasts FAQs


### What's a teardrop breast shape?


A teardrop breast is fuller at the bottom with a narrower, tapered top and significant forward projection from the chest wall. The shape sits lower on the chest than round breast shapes and extends further outward. Most bra fit issues for this shape trace back to that projection depth, not cup size.


### What's the difference between teardrop and bell shape?


Both shapes carry fullness at the bottom, but a bell shape is wider at the base with less forward projection. Teardrop breasts project further from the chest wall with a narrower, more tapered profile. The distinction matters for bra fit because teardrop shapes need deeper cups, while bell shapes need wider cups.


### What fit issues are common for teardrop breasts?


The most common: gaping at the top of the cup, underwire sitting on breast tissue instead of the chest wall, and molded cups that flatten projection rather than following it. These happen because standard bras are built for average projection depth. The fix is a cup designed for forward depth and a wire, like the CloudWire, that bends to follow the chest wall.


### What are the recommended bra styles for teardrop breasts?


Look for bras with flexible wire construction, deep cups, and seam placement that follows a bottom-full contour rather than shallow, molded cups or rigid underwire. The Honeylove CloudEmbrace with CloudWire is engineered for this shape with underwire support, while the CloudEmbrace wireless works well for lighter support needs. Unlined or seamed cups generally accommodate projection better than molded foam cups.
